newsitem.title: USA: BPA raises Friday peak, firm power $0.25/MWh.
newsitem.headline: BPA raises Friday peak, firm power $0.25/MWh.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) raised prices for firm power delivered during peak demand hours on Friday by 25 cents per megawatt hour (MWh), the agency said Thursday.
BPA still offered 300 megawatts of firm peak power, but raised prices to $15.75 per megawatt hour (MWh) for Northwest sales and $16.75 for California-Oregon border (COB) sales.
Prices for non-firm power during shoulder hours on Friday (0600, 1100-1700 and 2100-2200 PST) were unchanged at $11.00 for Northwest and $12.00 for COB.
BPA continued to refrain from offering non-firm power during morning and evening peaks or any displacement power.
Prices for firm and non-firm power during off-peak hours on Friday were unchanged at $9.00 per MWh for all deliveries.
